plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY02 rehearsing spoken texts with features of voice; VC2E5LY11 re-reading and editing for the ear; VC2E5LY01 giving and using feedback
plan.shape: model, guide, apply: the teacher edits the shade-trees speech by ear and models useful feedback, students fix tricky lines and name delivery fixes, then rehearse in trios and make final changes
plan.criticalFeature: practise the hard parts, not the whole thing again: find where you trip, fix it, say it three times
decisionPoints: the choice check: the feedback that helps most
the exit board: one specific grow for a new speaker
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it. Today: make Say it smooth.
plan.catchUp: Students without a finished speech rehearse their opening and finish only.

slides.notes: Open Week 9. One line: tomorrow is Speech Day. Today we make it smooth.

Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers, the Supported Worksheet for those who need it, and two Speech Feedback Cards per student. A timer per trio. Spread trios around the room and corridor.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to rehearse and refine a speech using feedback.
successCriteria: I can find and fix a line that is hard to say.
I can give and use specific feedback to improve my delivery.
I can plan gestures and a plan for nerves.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Speakers don't just practise. They practise the hard parts.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: How do the pros practise?
lines: A pianist doesn't play the whole song fifty times.
They find the tricky bars and play those, again and again.

notes.answer: practise the hard parts, not the whole thing again
beats: SAY: Athletes and musicians practise the hard bits most.
ASK: Think of a sport or skill. What do you practise most?
1 the easy part, 2 the hard part.
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 2
ASK: What would the hard part of your speech be?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: the story; the facts; looking up
SAY: Today you find your tricky lines and fix them.
trap: rehearsing by reading the whole speech silently.
Fix: say rehearsal is out loud, or it isn't rehearsal.

slides.meaning: To practise a performance out loud before the real thing.
slides.example: We rehearse in trios before Speech Day.

notes.answer: to practise a performance out loud before the real thing
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Rehearse. Say it with me. Rehearse.
SAY: To practise a performance out loud before the real thing.
SAY: We rehearse in trios before Speech Day.
ASK: What is the difference between reading and rehearsing?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: rehearsing is out loud, standing, like the real thing
trap: Fix: say out loud, standing, with your cards.

rows: Shade cuts UV by 75 per cent.
I read my action off the card.
Look up. Say it to their eyes.

notes.answer: say it aloud, mark the trip, fix it, say it three times
beats: SAY: Watch me say my speech out loud. Count my trips.
PERFORM the shade speech; stumble on the UV line.
POINT to row 1.
SAY: I tripped on a written line. So I swap it for words I'd say.
POINT to rows 2 and 3.
SAY: Some trips are delivery. Fix them, then say that bit three times.
ASK: How many times did I trip?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 3
trap: fixing a trip once and moving on.
Fix: say it three times smooth before it counts.
notes.stretch: Plan a gesture for your strongest line.
notes.help: Trip test only your opening and your finish.
notes.prep: Perform the stumbles on purpose. Critical feature: practise the hard parts.

slides.title: Delivery doctor
slides.pivot: act each one out, then ask what went wrong
slides.followUp: cold call one student: what's the fix?

items.text: Ava's speech took 50 seconds. 1 too fast, 2 too quiet, 3 no eye contact
The back row kept saying pardon? 1 too fast, 2 too quiet, 3 no eye contact
Ben read every word off his card. 1 too fast, 2 too quiet, 3 no eye contact
Lily whispered her call to action. 1 too fast, 2 too quiet, 3 no eye contact
Jack stared at the ceiling. 1 too fast, 2 too quiet, 3 no eye contact

say: One finger: too fast. Two: too quiet. Three: no eye contact.
trap: Fix: ask could they hear it, or could they keep up?
notes.help: Picture yourself in the back row.

options.text: Slow down in your story. Pause after 41 degrees.

options.misconception: too late, and not about delivery

notes.answer: B - specific: what, where, how to fix
beats: SAY: Three coaches give feedback after a rehearsal.
ASK: Which feedback helps most?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: what makes B useful?
Less -> ask which one could you fix tonight? re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. It says what, where and how. Coach like that today.
trap: pointing to A because it's nicest.
Fix: say kind and specific, both. Nice alone can't be fixed.
notes.prep: Decision point before trios. Under 80% means model one more coach comment together.

slides.title: Trip test
slides.pivot: say it aloud, circle the trip word, swap it
slides.followUp: cold call one board: say it smoothly three times

items.answer: e.g. So the problem is still here.
e.g. Three out of four of us agreed.
e.g. More and more animals are in danger.

say: Make each line easy to say out loud.
trap: swapping one long word for another long word.
Fix: student says it aloud; if they trip, swap again.
notes.stretch: Add a stressed word in capitals.

slides.title: Trio rehearsals
lines: Speaker: give your speech from your cue cards.
Timer: time it. Coach: fill in the Feedback Card.
Rotate until everyone has spoken, then fix and go again.

notes.answer: open - every student rehearses and gets one glow and one grow
beats: SAY: Trios. Speaker, timer, coach. Then rotate.
TIME the rounds: 4 minutes each including feedback.
CIRCULATE. Listen for one great grow comment to share.
ASK: Thumbs: did your coach give you a grow you can fix tonight?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: mostly thumbs up
ASK: Tell your coach the one change you'll make.
15 sec. Turn and tell, speaker first.
EXPECT: a specific change
trap: coaches writing good job as the grow.
Fix: coach must name a line or a moment.
notes.stretch: Second run: add a gesture to your strongest line.
notes.help: Rehearse just the opening and finish first.
notes.prep: Fun activity: trio rehearsal with Feedback Cards. 14 minutes. SC2.

slides.title: Refine my speech
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Finish by writing your three final changes, then make them on your speech and cards.

notes.answer: three specific changes from the trip test and feedback
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Make your three changes on your real speech and cards.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: show me a line you fixed. Say it three times.
ASK: Say your fixed line to your partner three times.
30 sec each. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: smoother each time
trap: writing changes but never saying them aloud.
Fix: student says each changed line three times.
notes.stretch: Extension: plan gestures, then a plan for nerves.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a fix done, a frame.
notes.prep: Independent refining; tomorrow is Speech Day. SC2.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in three final changes made to the student's speech

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: A speaker stares at their shoes and mumbles their final line.
Write one specific grow comment for them.

notes.answer: e.g. Look up and say your final line loudly to the back wall.
beats: SAY: A new speaker. Coach them in one line.
ASK: Write one specific grow comment.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: what, where and how to fix
RECORD who writes a vague comment. Pair them with a strong coach on Speech Day.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: What is the one line you'll practise tonight?

notes.answer: open - a named line from their speech
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How ready do you feel for Speech Day?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: What is the one line you'll practise tonight?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: a named line from their speech
notes.prep: Speeches and cards go home to practise tonight, or stay in the folder. SC2.
